summary: Chinese video course with PyTorch and TensorFlow code for classic vision networks, from LeNet and ResNet to YOLO, U-Net and Vision Transformer.

sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: This is a tutorial series on deep learning for images, organized from the author's graduate research and shared as videos (in Chinese, on Bilibili) with matching code. For each network it explains the structure and key ideas, then builds and trains it in PyTorch and, for many, TensorFlow/Keras. Topics cover image classification, object detection, semantic segmentation, instance segmentation and keypoint detection.
sixtySeconds.problem: Papers on vision models are hard to turn into working code. This series walks through each network and shows a full implementation.
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it for a large, structured set of explained implementations, with slides for every lesson in the course_ppt folder.
requirements: Chinese for the videos (the code is readable without them)

overview: Classification covers LeNet, AlexNet, VGG, GoogLeNet, ResNet, ResNeXt, MobileNet, ShuffleNet, EfficientNet, RepVGG, Vision Transformer, Swin Transformer, ConvNeXt and MobileViT.
Detection covers Faster R-CNN/FPN, SSD/RetinaNet, the YOLO series and FCOS; segmentation covers FCN, DeepLabV3, LR-ASPP, U-Net, U2Net and Mask R-CNN; keypoints cover DeepPose and HRNet.
Each topic links to explanation and source-code walkthrough videos. Slides are in course_ppt. It is GPL-3.0 licensed.
limitations: Videos and README are in Chinese
